title: Domestic proportion beyond binding equality

captions.physics: Maintaining familiar comfort at freedom’s expense
captions.energy: Equalising efforts without considering their content
captions.emotions: Feeling proportion between needs and capacity

meaning: Your domestic support keeps its measure when both can review the binding quantity itself instead of merely dividing more precisely work already excessive for each.
text: The Devil in the physical position of Muladhara describes domestic actions maintaining familiar comfort even at the cost of free choice. Justice in energy intensifies them through literal equalisation. Temperance in emotions feels suitable measure. Division can look fair without becoming manageable. Both share the entire earlier workload equally, but its scale remains untouchable. An inward sense of proportion conflicts less with someone’s share than with preserving comfort already requiring too much maintenance from shared domestic life.

For example, numerous houseplants receive equally shared care. Both find it heavy, but discussion concerns only more precise turns while pot quantity apparently cannot shrink. **Suitable measure includes reviewing the total load even when it is divided equally.** Actual usefulness can be named and enough chosen. Support returns to both without fairness indefinitely maintaining a familiar quantity merely because it already received a flawlessly symmetrical distribution scheme.

The difficulty is considering reduction less responsible than precise performance. Shares match while willing participation diminishes. Distinguishing equality from manageability offers more dependable support: one does not guarantee the other. Home supports both through choosing present measure according to actual capacity instead of making fair division grounds for retaining every binding habit regardless of its future usefulness to shared life. A smaller total can preserve clear responsibility rather than weaken it.
